we can eliminate the last rule-based step from Neural Belief Tracking, and that this model can be trained end-to-end with a very small additional number of parameters.

we can learn a data-driven belief update mechanism for NBT that achieves competitive performance in three languages, and that this mechanism can be learned with a small amount of additional model parameters.

(a) a fully data-driven NBT model is competitive to the best performing NBT models in the literature, (b) this model is more robust to the size of the training data, and (c) this model can be easily adapted to new dialogue domains.

the following question: Can a data-driven model be used to replace a rule-based module in a data-driven dialogue state tracker?
the following question: How can we build an effective data-driven dialogue state tracker that is not only robust to new domains, but is also easy to deploy and maintain?

The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple statistical model can replace a rule-based belief tracking mechanism, which can significantly simplify the model development and deployment process.
we can now learn the belief tracking model jointly with the other components of the DST system and eliminate the need for a rule-based belief state update mechanism.

a fully statistical model can achieve comparable performance to rule-based models, which is an important step towards the goal of building data-driven DST models that can be deployed to a variety of domains.
